learningObjectives: Understand the basic concepts behind TestSheets.
Identify the differences between Attributes and Instances.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Scenario: Testing the Shirt Size Selector

elements.text: Independent scenario: a sample product accepts sizes S, M and L and rejects XL. Design input values and expected results for each path. This is a hypothetical specification, not a verified statement about the current Demo Web Shop catalogue or its UI ability to submit an unavailable size.

elements.description: A TestSheet organizes test data into a logical testing structure. It can use Attributes for data-oriented cases or Steps for process-oriented cases; it is not itself a completed execution run.

elements.title: Create a TestSheet
items: In TestCase-Design, right-click a folder and choose Create TestSheet.
Choose a name unique within that folder and add the required structure.
Agree the input and expected-result data with the relevant business stakeholders.

elements.description: An Attribute represents a business object characteristic and can contain sub-Attributes or Instances. Its icon color reflects business relevance, which can be changed; do not identify its meaning solely from a fixed red icon.
An Instance supplies a concrete variant. Attribute-level variants supply values; TestSheet-level Instances describe complete combinations for later generation.

elements.caption: Independent value-domain illustration. A matching data combination and template generation are needed to create an automated TestCase; each shown value box is not already one.

elements.text: If you can only see Attributes and not Instances, press F9 — it hides/unhides all Instances in the TestCaseDesign (red) section of Tosca.

elements.title: Add Attributes and Instances
items: Create the required Attributes and their value Instances.
Create TestSheet-level combinations manually or generate them with an appropriate method.
Review expected outputs and combination coverage before linking the TestSheet to a Template.

elements.description: Straight Through is the Instance Character for the frequently used path with fewest dependencies; it is required for linear expansion. ValidValues can be an example name, but neither that name nor the leftmost column position makes an Instance Straight Through. Set Character deliberately.

elements.text: Invalid describes input expected to trigger an error; it is not an execution failure status. A negative test can pass when the specified rejection and every other assertion succeed. It may fail for a missing error, wrong message or another failed assertion—not only when invalid input is accepted.

bulletPoints: The independent example has four size variants; build and inspect their combinations before generation.

elements.text: Design three hypothetical users with Email and Password Attributes. Put each complete user combination at TestSheet level and associate the intended values. Use synthetic data. Academy exercise instructions and downloadable workspace subsets were inaccessible and have not been verified.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing an Invalid Instance with a failing TestCase
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume any TestCase built from an 'invalid' Instance is expected to fail.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Invalid input is not a failed execution status. Check the expected rejection and all other assertions.

examPitfalls.title: Not knowing the F9 shortcut
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Learners can't find Instances in a limited TestCaseDesign view and assume the TestSheet is broken.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Press F9 in the TestCaseDesign (red) section to show/hide all Instances alongside Attributes.

examPitfalls.title: Character and relevance are properties
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming a column name or fixed icon color defines business meaning.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect Character and BusinessRelevant properties rather than relying on a name or color.

examPitfalls.title: Adding Instances at the wrong level
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Placing complete hypothetical user combinations under only Email or Password.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Instances added directly on the TestSheet (right-click the TestSheet itself) represent the individual TestCases/users — e.g. User1, User2, User3. Instances added under an Attribute represent that Attribute's specific values.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is a TestSheet in Tosca terminology?

options.text: The basic framework of TestCase-Design, made of Attributes and Instances that specify the combinations to test.
A report generated only after ExecutionList runs.
A spreadsheet exported from Excel that Tosca cannot edit directly.
A single TestCase renamed for reuse.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's created inside the TestCaseDesign folder.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A TestSheet is the basic framework of TestCase-Design: Attributes and Instances, in a structured way, specify the different combinations of TestCases needed.

optionExplanations.A: A TestSheet structures data and combinations before automation and execution.
optionExplanations.B: An execution report records results rather than designing these combinations.
optionExplanations.C: Tosca creates and edits native TestSheets; Excel import is not their definition.
optionExplanations.D: Renaming a test does not create a TestCase-Design data structure.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In TestCase-Design, what does an Attribute represent?

options.text: A concrete variant, equivalent to an Instance.
A business object characteristic, potentially containing sub-Attributes or Instances.
Only a TestStepValue reference.
Only the name of an ExecutionList.

practiceQuiz.hint: Instances are the variants; Attributes are the features.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Attributes represent characteristics; their icon color depends on BusinessRelevant, not one universal color.

optionExplanations.A: A concrete variant is an Instance rather than the Attribute itself.
optionExplanations.B: An Attribute represents a characteristic and can have nested structure or values.
optionExplanations.C: Its role is broader than a reference to a TestStepValue.
optionExplanations.D: ExecutionList naming belongs to execution organization, not this data characteristic.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In an independent negative-test example, XL is specified as invalid input. The SUT returns the exact expected rejection and every other assertion succeeds. What result is expected?

options.text: The result is inconclusive and must be manually reviewed every time.
The TestCase FAILS, because an Invalid Instance always causes a TestCase failure.
The TestCase is skipped automatically.
The TestCase PASSES, because the SUT correctly rejected the invalid value as expected.

practiceQuiz.hint: Failing = actual values differ from expected. Here, the expected outcome (rejection) occurred.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Invalid input can lead to a passed test when every specified assertion, including the rejection, succeeds.

optionExplanations.A: The scenario specifies all assertions succeeded, so no inconclusive result is implied.
optionExplanations.B: Input Character Invalid does not itself set execution status to Failed.
optionExplanations.C: Invalid input does not automatically skip the test.
optionExplanations.D: All required assertions, including rejection, succeeded in this scenario.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You only see Attributes in the TestCaseDesign section, not the Instances beneath them. How do you reveal the Instances?

options.text: Instances cannot be hidden; something else is wrong.
Right-click the TestSheet and select 'Refresh'.
Press F9 to toggle Instance visibility.
Restart Tosca Commander.

practiceQuiz.rationale: F9 hides/unhides all Instances in the TestCaseDesign (red) section of Tosca.

optionExplanations.A: Instances can be hidden by the active visibility setting.
optionExplanations.B: Refreshing is not the visibility-toggle command specified here.
optionExplanations.C: F9 toggles Instance visibility in the active TestCase-Design context.
optionExplanations.D: Restarting is unnecessary to change this visibility setting.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How do you designate a Straight Through value for the representative path?

options.text: Set the Instance Character to Straight Through; this does not depend on naming a leftmost column ValidValues.
'Verification' — it only holds expected output values.
'ExecutionList' — it links directly to the Execution section.
'Defaults' — a column Tosca auto-generates and cannot be edited.

practiceQuiz.hint: Inspect the Instance property rather than its grid position.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Straight Through is an Instance Character, not an automatic property of a column position or example name.

optionExplanations.A: Character explicitly designates Straight Through; grid position or naming does not.
optionExplanations.B: Expected-output use is separate from Straight Through Character.
optionExplanations.C: An ExecutionList is a separate execution container.
optionExplanations.D: A fixed uneditable Defaults column is not the documented Character mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where do you create a new TestSheet, and how?

options.text: TestSheets are auto-generated the first time a Template is instantiated.
Right-click the TestCaseDesign folder → Create TestSheet.
Import it directly from an Excel file — Tosca cannot create one natively.
Right-click the ExecutionList folder → Create TestSheet.

practiceQuiz.hint: It lives in the TestCaseDesign section, alongside Attributes and Instances.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A TestSheet is created by right-clicking the TestCaseDesign folder and selecting Create TestSheet, then manually adding Attributes and Instances.

optionExplanations.A: A native TestSheet can be created before a Template is instantiated.
optionExplanations.B: Create TestSheet is available on a TestCase-Design folder.
optionExplanations.C: Native creation is supported; importing Excel is not mandatory.
optionExplanations.D: ExecutionList folders are not where the TestCase-Design command creates TestSheets.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What are the keyboard shortcuts to create a new Attribute and a new Instance, respectively?

options.text: Ctrl+A for a new Attribute; Ctrl+I for a new Instance (no prefix needed).
Ctrl+N, Ctrl+T for both — Tosca does not differentiate the two.
F9 for a new Attribute; F10 for a new Instance.
Ctrl+N, Ctrl+A for a new Attribute; Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I for a new Instance.

practiceQuiz.hint: Both start with the same Ctrl+N prefix, then a second letter to specify what's being created.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The current TestCase-Design object documentation lists Ctrl+N, Ctrl+A for Attribute and Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I for Instance; this does not certify an original exercise workbook.

optionExplanations.A: The creation commands require the stated Ctrl+N chord rather than these standalone keys.
optionExplanations.B: Ctrl+N, Ctrl+T creates a TestSheet in this context, not both object types.
optionExplanations.C: F9 controls visibility and does not create an Attribute.
optionExplanations.D: These are the documented creation chords for the two object types.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In an independent login-data example, where should you create complete combinations User1, User2 and User3 with their own Email and Password values?

options.text: In a separate TestSheet, one per user.
Directly on the TestSheet itself (not under the Email or Password Attribute).
Under the Password Attribute only.
Under the Email Attribute only.

practiceQuiz.hint: This is the same distinction as 'Instance on TestSheet level = TestCase' from the core lesson.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Instances created directly on the TestSheet (right-click the TestSheet itself) represent the individual TestCases/users — User1, User2, User3. The Email/Password Instances underneath the Attributes hold each user's specific values, set via drop-down in the TestSheet grid.

optionExplanations.A: One sheet per user is unnecessary for three combinations in the same structure.
optionExplanations.B: Top-level Instances represent the complete user combinations.
optionExplanations.C: A Password variant alone does not describe a complete Email/Password user combination.
optionExplanations.D: An Email variant alone likewise does not represent the entire user.

quickRecap.value: Central, structured repository of test data (Attributes + Instances) for TestCase-Design.
Business characteristic; inspect BusinessRelevant rather than assuming a fixed icon color.
A variant of an Attribute (white box, capital 'I') — e.g. S, M, L, XL.
Toggles Instance visibility in the TestCaseDesign section.
Straight Through is an Instance Character, not a reserved leftmost-column name.
Negative input can pass when the expected rejection and all other assertions succeed.
Ctrl+N, Ctrl+A = new Attribute. Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I = new Instance.
Instance on the TestSheet itself = a TestCase/user. Instance under an Attribute = that Attribute's value.
